::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Status: design. No probe has run.

Written against [the design standard](../studies/DESIGN-STANDARD.md).

**Disclosure.** This study could show that estimates from studies built on PMC full text are
biased upward. That includes this project's own P01, P01v2 and P02, and the author's published
transparency studies (PMIDs 36482006, 37494359), which used the same kind of sample. The
instrument, `rtransparency`, is maintained by the author.
:::

## 1. The question

Text-mining meta-research, this project included, reads full text from the PMC open-access
subset because that is the full text a script can legally fetch. Being open access is itself a
transparency behavior. If openly available articles are also likelier to disclose conflicts, name
funders and share data, then every prevalence estimated from PMC full text is too high, and the
field's picture of its own progress is flattering.

This project found the first sign of it. Probe P2 of P01v2 measured PMC coverage at 77.7 percent
among articles about data sharing against 57.8 percent among others: which articles reach PMC
depends on what they are about.

## 2. Prior work, and the search behind the novelty claim

Log key `P13`.

```
corpus regex: (open access|PubMed Central|PMC).{0,80}(sampl|selection).{0,40}
              (bias|represent).{0,80}(transparen|disclos|sharing)
PubMed:       ("open access"[tiab] OR "PubMed Central"[tiab]) AND ("selection bias"[tiab]
              OR representativeness[tiab] OR "sampling bias"[tiab]) AND (transparency[tiab]
              OR "conflict of interest"[tiab] OR "data sharing"[tiab] OR funding[tiab])
              AND (meta-research[tiab] OR "research on research"[tiab] OR bibliometric*[tiab]
              OR "text mining"[tiab])
```

**Zero** PubMed records and zero corpus records.

## 3. Hypothesis

Within the same journal and year, articles in the PMC open-access subset carry transparency
indicators more often than articles that are not.

**Null.** The within-journal-year odds ratio, PMC open access against not, is 1.

**What would falsify it.** An odds ratio at or below 1, which would mean PMC-based estimates are
not biased upward on this axis and the field's samples are safer than feared.

## 4. Design and unit

Cross-sectional comparison, matched on journal and publication year. One article is one unit.

## 5. Sample

Journals indexed in PubMed that publish both PMC open-access and non-PMC articles in the same
year, 2018 to 2024. Within each journal-year, every PMC open-access article and an equal number
of non-PMC articles sampled at random; a journal-year with fewer non-PMC articles contributes all
of them and is weighted (S9).

## 6. Exposure

Membership of the PMC open-access subset, from the PMC OA file list at a dated snapshot.

## 7. Outcome and instrument

Two tiers, because the comparison arm has no PMC full text by definition.

**Tier 1, every article.** Indicators PubMed records in metadata for any article whatever its
access: a `CoiStatement` element, a `GrantList`, and a registry identifier in `DataBankList`.
These are read from PubMed XML and do not depend on full text. That makes the comparison fair and
also narrow: PubMed metadata records what publishers deposit, and deposit practice may differ by
access status, which is a threat in its own right (section 10).

**Tier 2, a subsample.** Full-text indicators from `rtransparency::rt_all` on non-PMC articles
whose full text is legally obtainable elsewhere: publisher-hosted open access outside PMC, and
author manuscripts in institutional repositories. PDFs are converted with `rt_read_pdf`. This is
the route to data and code sharing, which metadata does not carry.

## 8. Validation gate

`rtransparency` accuracy on PDFs converted to text is not the published accuracy on PMC XML. The
author codes 100 tier 2 articles blind to the detector's output. **Detector sensitivity is
computed separately for XML and PDF input; if they differ by more than 0.10, tier 2 comparisons
report input-specific corrected estimates only** (S3).

## 9. Analysis

In R.

```r
clogit(indicator ~ in_pmc_oa + strata(journal_year), data = d)
```

One model per indicator. Preregistered alongside: a probabilistic bias analysis for tier 2 using
the section 8 accuracies, and the implied inflation of a PMC-only prevalence estimate,
computed as the difference between the PMC-only and the reweighted all-access prevalence.

## 10. Threats

| threat | handling | removed or disclosed | standard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Publishers deposit metadata differently by access status | The central threat to tier 1; tier 2 exists partly to check it | Disclosed | |
| PDF text degrades detection | Accuracy measured per input type; corrected estimates when they differ | Disclosed | S3 |
| Non-PMC full text that is obtainable is itself selected | Tier 2 compares PMC against the obtainable part of non-PMC, which is a lower bound on the gap | Disclosed | |
| Journal and year confound access and practice | Matched and conditioned on journal-year | Removed | S9 |
| The author maintains the instrument and his own results are at stake | Stated at the top; the gate's coding is blind to detector output | Disclosed | |

## 11. Probes

| probe | computes | goes to | what would change the design | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PA** | journal-years with both PMC OA and non-PMC articles, and article counts | 5 | too few mixed journal-years forces a between-journal design with its confounding | not run |
| **PB** | presence rate of each PubMed metadata field, marginally, not by access | 7 | a field present in under 20 percent of all records cannot carry the comparison | not run |
| **PC** | legally obtainable non-PMC full text for 200 sampled articles | 7 | under 30 percent obtainable makes tier 2 a small, selected subsample and it is labeled exploratory | not run |
| **PD** | the author's 100 blind codings | 8 | input-specific accuracy triggers corrected estimates | needs the author |

## 12. What this cannot show

- The size of the bias for indicators neither tier can see.
- Whether the bias has changed over time, which would matter for trend studies; a stated
  extension, not part of this design.
